$comment: What a saved dashboard is, on the wire and on disk.
jarvis-core's tests/test_dashboards.py and the console's
src/lib/dashboards/layout.test.ts both read this file. A layout written by
one and refused by the other is the failure it exists to prevent: the
console is not the only client (the phone loads the same console), and a
layout is the one piece of state a user builds by hand and would be angry
to lose.
Coordinates are a 12-column grid. `w`/`h` are in columns and rows; a row is
whatever height the console draws it at, which is a display decision and
deliberately not stored.
A widget has a `kind` (M63). `metric` is the graphs of M62 and the default
when the field is absent, so every layout saved before kinds existed still
loads. The other kinds show the house rather than a number: one entity's
state with its switch, the newest sensor readings by room, a still from a
camera, the sky tonight, the newest moments. Each kind names the fields it
needs under `kinds`; a widget missing one is refused, not drawn blank.

fields.title: what the user called it
fields.owner: the token id that saved it — see `owner` below
fields.widgets: array, in no particular order; `x`/`y` decide the layout
fields.range: the window the dashboard opens on: 1h | 6h | 24h | 7d
fields.order: shipped only: which example opens first — lowest first, then file name

fields.title: optional; the widget's own subject is used when absent
fields.type: metric: one of `types` below; absent means line
fields.source: metric: a data source name: internal | influx | …; absent means internal
fields.series: metric: array of series keys, as that source lists them
fields.aggregate: metric: last | mean | min | max | sum | count
fields.entity: entity: the entity_id the tile shows and switches
fields.camera: camera: the camera's name; absent means the only camera, if there is one
fields.area: readings: only this room; absent means every room
fields.limit: moments: how many, newest first (1-20, default 6)

entity.what: one entity: name, state with unit, when it changed, and its switch when it has one

readings.what: the newest sensor readings, grouped by room

camera.what: a still from a camera, through the vision integration's consent and audit

sky.what: the next ISS pass and the moon tonight

moments.what: the newest moments — what Jarvis said while nobody was looking

types.area: the same, filled — for a quantity rather than a level
types.stat: one number, large, with an optional sparkline
types.table: several series' latest values, side by side

$comment: There are no user accounts (jarvis/auth.py:3). A token IS the identity:
one per device, minted by the operator. So a dashboard belongs to the
token that saved it, and 'per user' means 'per token id'. A layout with no
owner is shared — the shipped examples are.

commands.jarvis/dashboards/list: every dashboard this token may see: its own, plus the shared ones
commands.jarvis/dashboards/save: create or replace one; the server stamps `owner` from the token
commands.jarvis/dashboards/delete: by id; refuses one this token does not own
commands.jarvis/metrics/sources: what can be graphed, per source
commands.jarvis/sensors/readings: readings: every sensor's newest reading with its room and age; `area` filters
commands.jarvis/sky/summary: sky: the next pass of the first tracked satellite and the moon tonight, or why not yet
commands.jarvis/vision/still: camera: one frame as a JPEG data URL, through the same consent, rate limit and audit as a look; refused without consent
